data.name: Jesiah
data.long_meaning: The name Jesiah comes from the Hebrew language and means 'God is salvation'. In the Bible, Jesiah is mentioned in the Old Testament as a descendant of King David and as a prophet. In Christian tradition, Jesiah is associated with the idea of God's salvation and protection.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jesiah carries rich cultural significance as it is rooted in the Hebrew language and the Old Testament tradition. It represents a connection to biblical history and Jewish heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: Jesiah holds immense spiritual significance as it signifies the belief in God's saving power and protection. It is a reminder of the Christian faith's central tenet of God's love and salvation for humanity. Jesiah, as the name implies, is a reflection of the hope and trust that God will deliver us from our troubles and offer us a better future.

historical_references.reference: The name Jesiah is believed to be a variant of the Hebrew name Jehoshia or Jehoshua, which means 'God will help'. This name is mentioned several times in the Old Testament, including in the books of Joshua and 1 Kings. The most famous bearer of this name is Joshua, who led the Israelites into the Promised Land according to the Hebrew Bible.
The name Jesiah is also mentioned in the New Testament as a name given to a descendant of King David in the genealogy of Jesus Christ. This is recorded in Matthew 1:8 and Luke 3:29.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Jesiah continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.

name_in_real_life.story: Thomas Jesiah from Rome, Italy embodies the meaning of Jesiah - "God is salvation". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Jesiah is believed to mean "God saves" or "Jehovah saves" in Hebrew, reflecting the Christian belief in divine intervention and salvation. It is a modern variation of the name Jesus, emphasizing the saving grace of God.
